'''Jeremy Allen Moss''' (born June 23, 1986) is an American politician from [[Southfield, Michigan]], currently representing [[Michigan's 7th Senate district]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=District |url=https://senatedems.com/moss/district/ |access-date=May 14, 2023 |website=Senator Jeremy Moss |language=en-US}}</ref> A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], Moss is the [[List of first openly LGBT politicians in the United States|first openly gay person]] elected to the [[Michigan Senate]], and the first to serve as its [[president pro tempore]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cappelletti |first=Joey |date=June 28, 2023 |title=Michigan Legislature approves ban on 'conversion therapy' for LGBTQ+ minors |url=https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/michigan-legislature-approves-ban-conversion-therapy-lgbtq-minors-100441782 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230630210145/https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/michigan-legislature-approves-ban-conversion-therapy-lgbtq-minors-100441782 |archive-date=June 30, 2023 |website=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]}}</ref> Moss represented [[Michigan's 35th House of Representatives district]] in the [[Michigan House of Representatives]] from 2014 to 2018.<ref name="e186">{{cite web | title=Michigan 35th District State House Results: Jeremy Moss Wins | website=The New York Times | date=November 8, 2016 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/elections/2016/results/michigan-state-house-district-35 | access-date=November 7, 2025}}</ref> Before running for the state legislature, Moss, at age 25, was elected to the Southfield City Council in 2011, becoming the youngest member elected in the body's history.<ref name="w013">{{cite web | title=Southfield Swearing In Youngest Councilman In City's History | website=CBS Detroit | date=November 21, 2011 | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/detroit/news/southfield-swearing-in-youngest-councilman-in-citys-history/ | access-date=November 7, 2025}}</ref><ref name="caucus_bio">{{Cite web |title=Biography For Rep. Moss |url=http://housedems.com/state-rep-jeremy-moss-biography |access-date=June 30, 2015 |work=Michigan House Democrats |archive-date=August 20, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170820042830/http://www.housedems.com/state-rep-jeremy-moss-biography |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="btl1114">{{Cite news |author=Trager, AJ |date=November 6, 2014 |title=Jeremy Moss: Next State House Rep. District 35 |work=Between The Lines |issue=2245 |url=http://www.pridesource.com/article.html?article=68881 |access-date=June 30, 2015}}</ref>

In 2026 Moss was elected as Michigan’s first openly gay member of Congress.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/11/03/democrat-jeremy-moss-11th-district-ethan-baker-haley-stevens-first-gay-member-election-results/92503366007/|title=Democrat Jeremy Moss wins to become Michigan's first gay congressman|first=Grant|last=Schwab|website=The Detroit News}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Jeremy Moss was born on June 23, 1986, in Detroit.<ref name="caucus_bio" /><ref name="btl1114" /> He attended [[Hillel Day School]] and graduated from [[Birmingham Groves High School|Wylie E. Groves High School]] in the Birmingham Public School District.<ref name="vfund-moss">{{Cite web | title = Jeremy Moss WINS Democratic Primary in Michigan | publisher = Gay & Lesbian Victory Fund | work = victoryfund.org | date = August 5, 2014 | author = Thai, Steven | access-date = June 30, 2015 | url = https://www.victoryfund.org/our-story/gay-politics-blog/jeremy-moss-wins-democratic-primary-michigan | archive-date = February 6, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170206084915/https://www.victoryfund.org/our-story/gay-politics-blog/jeremy-moss-wins-democratic-primary-michigan | url-status = dead }}</ref>

He graduated with high honors from [[Michigan State University]] with a bachelor's degree in [[journalism]] and an additional major in [[political science]].{{Page needed|date=August 2025}} He graduated from the Michigan Political Leadership Program Fellowship.<ref name="caucus_bio" /><ref name="vfund-moss" />

==Career==
Moss worked in the offices of Mayor [[Brenda Lawrence]] and State Representative [[Paul Condino]].<ref name="btl1114" /><ref name="btl1213">{{Cite interview | title = State Rep. Candidate Jeremy Moss | author = Proxmire, Crystal A. | work = Between The Lines | date = December 5, 2013 | access-date = June 30, 2015 |url=https://pridesource.com/article/59263/ }}</ref> He worked as district director for State Representative [[Rudy Hobbs]]<ref name="vfund-moss" /> after serving as his [[campaign manager]].<ref name="btl1213" />

In November 2011, at age 25,<ref name="btl1213" /> he placed first among eight candidates to be elected to serve as the youngest-ever elected official in Southfield.<ref name="caucus_bio" /><ref name="vfund-moss" /> He served as [[chairman]] of the council's Legislative and Urban Affairs Committee, and as a member of the Boards and Commission and Neighborhood Services committees. In 2013, Moss successfully advocated for the creation of a new Economic Development Committee.<ref name="vfund-moss" />

He was elected to serve the [[Michigan's 35th House of Representatives district|35th District]] in the Michigan House of Representatives in November 2014.<ref name="mlive1114">{{cite news |date=November 4, 2014 |title=2014 Live Michigan election results: State House Districts 1-110 |work=MLive |url=https://www.mlive.com/politics/index.ssf/2014/11/2014_live_michigan_election_re_3.html |access-date=June 30, 2015}}</ref> He became the second openly gay member elected to the Michigan legislature.<ref name="vfund-moss"/>

In his first term in the Michigan House of Representatives, he served as minority vice chairman of the House Local Government Committee and sat on the House Commerce and Trade and House Regulatory Reform committees.<ref name="caucus_bio" /><ref name="bpedia-moss">{{Cite web | title = Jeremy Moss | publisher = Ballotpedia | work = ballotpedia.org | access-date = June 30, 2015 |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Jeremy_Moss }}</ref>

Moss was re-elected in 2016. His colleagues selected him to serve as the House Democratic [[Whip (politics)|Whip]]. In his second term, he served as minority vice chairman of the House Regulatory Reform Committee and sat on the House Elections and Ethics Committee, House Local Government Committee, and the Joint Committee on Administrative Rules.<ref name="caucus_bio" />

In 2018, Moss was elected to represent the 11th Michigan Senate District and was the Assistant Democratic Leader. Moss started his second term in the Michigan Senate in 2023, representing district 7.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Committees |url=https://senatedems.com/moss/committees/ |access-date=June 30, 2023 |website=Senator Jeremy Moss |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2026 Moss was elected as Michigan’s first openly gay member of Congress.<ref name="auto"/>

== Political positions ==
Moss supports [[Israel]] and a [[two-state solution]], while opposing [[Benjamin Netanyahu]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 5, 2026 |title=Pro-Israel Jewish Democrat Jeremy Moss Wins Michigan Congressional Primary |url=https://www.haaretz.com/us-news/2026-08-05/ty-article/.premium/jeremy-moss-wins-michigan-democratic-congressional-primary/0000019f-d0d7-d147-adff-f1ff0a520000 |website=Haaretz}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Moss is a lifelong resident of [[Southfield, Michigan]].<ref name="caucus_bio" /><ref name="btl1114" /> He is a member of the Greater Southfield/Farmington chapter of the [[National Association for the Advancement of Colored People]] and the Martin Luther King Task Force, and is a board member of Congregation Beth Ahm in [[Oakland County, Michigan|Oakland County]].<ref name="caucus_bio" />

Moss is [[Jewish]] and [[openly gay]].<ref name="vfund-moss"/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Gerstein |first1=Michael |title=Rep: 'Foreign law' bill could cut Jewish circumcisions |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2017/04/20/bill-ban-foreign-laws-michigan/100692498/ |website=www.detroitnews.com |publisher=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=August 26, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Runkle |first1=Anne |title=Sen. Moss of Southfield is lead sponsor of proposed LGBTQ protections in civil rights act |url=https://www.theoaklandpress.com/news/local/sen-moss-of-southfield-is-lead-sponsor-of-proposed-lgbtq/article_5e105966-8719-11e9-a706-0fc35f0dd421.html |website=www.theoaklandpress.com |publisher=[[The Oakland Press]] |access-date=August 26, 2019 |archive-date=January 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122082630/https://www.theoaklandpress.com/news/local/sen-moss-of-southfield-is-lead-sponsor-of-proposed-lgbtq/article_5e105966-8719-11e9-a706-0fc35f0dd421.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is a fan of singer and actress [[Patti LaBelle]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Knoppow |first=Ellen Shanna |title="I didn't lose consciousness": Gay lawmaker on his resilience as he runs for Congress |url=https://www.lgbtqnation.com/2026/01/i-didnt-lose-consciousness-gay-lawmaker-on-his-resilience-as-he-runs-for-congress/ |access-date=April 14, 2026 |website=[[LGBTQ Nation]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Electoral history==
In 2014, he defeated Nicole Brown, Darryle Buchanan, and Charles Roddis in the Democratic primary for the 35th District of the Michigan House of Representatives on August 5, 2014. He then went on to defeat [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] candidate Robert Brim in the general election on November 4, 2014.<ref name="mlive1114" /><ref name="bpedia-moss" /> He defeated Brim in a rematch in 2016.

In 2018, Moss defeated Crystal Bailey, Vanessa Moss, and James Turner in the Democratic primary for the 11th State Senate district.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/pages/interactives/freep/election-results/primary/2018/oakland/|title=2018 Michigan Primary Election: Oakland County results|website=Detroit Free Press}}</ref> He went on to defeat Republican Boris Tuman and [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]] James Young in the general election.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/election-results/michigan-general-election-results-for-state-senate-district-11-on-nov-6-2018|title=Michigan General Election Results for State Senate District 11 on Nov. 6, 2018|first=Ken|last=Haddad|date=October 10, 2018|website=WDIV}}</ref>

Following the 2022 [[Redistricting in Michigan|redistricting]], Moss successfully ran for re-election in the newly drawn 7th Michigan Senate District and served as the Michigan Senate Democratic campaign co-chair as the caucus won its first majority in 40 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/2022-midterm-elections-abortion-pennsylvania-nevada-minnesota-16dfb0f76ac9cf6fc781b44fa3f239fc|title=Democrats buck midterm history to win control of 4 states|first=David A.|last=Lieb|date=November 9, 2022|website=Associated Press}}</ref>
